correctness.rationale: The complete set of optimal truncations follows from the explicit spectrum and Eckart–Young–Mirsky. Since 0≤P≤I, every off-diagonal projector entry is at least −1/2, and a zero-sum projector containing (e1−e2)/sqrt(2) attains the bound for every intermediate rank. Partition projectors supply strictly positive rank-r matrices with explicit nonnegative factors and exactly the optimal Frobenius error. Adding epsilon times the attaining projector separates the spectrum, keeps all input entries positive, forces a unique negative-entry optimum, and yields the strict constrained gap by uniqueness plus a closed feasible set; a partition competitor bounds the penalty by epsilon sqrt(r−1). The dimensional proof is symbolic and exact. 36 dimension/rank rational checks and the n=3 illustration passed; these checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic searches compared equivalent formulations, dominating parameter statements, numeric tables, and implication relations. Relevant complete texts were inspected, particularly the 2022 randomized low-rank nonnegative approximation study, the 2020 tangent-space alternating projections study, and the 2009 singular-value nonnegativity-perturbation criteria. These study algorithms or sufficient preservation conditions and do not establish the sharp all-tie, all-intermediate-rank compound-symmetric criterion together with zero NMF cost and the vanishing-cost spectral-gap perturbation. The classical spectral and projector ingredients are acknowledged, and absence of indexed direct coverage is not regarded as proof of priority.
residual_risks: Unlocated specialized theorems on entrywise sign of degenerate truncated SVDs or nonnegative best low-rank approximations might imply parts of the theorem.
Novelty is a combined exact structural classification with standard spectral tools; independent publication-priority assessment is outstanding.

value.rationale: Nonnegative low-rank approximation and the distinction between truncated SVD and nonnegative-factorizable optimization are practical numerical-analysis questions. The theorem identifies a precise dimension-scaled parameter threshold independent of truncation rank, shows that the nonnegative constraint can cost nothing even where some unconstrained minimizers are negative, and proves a robust sign-versus-objective-cost separation after arbitrarily small data perturbation. These exact structural facts offer benchmarks for tie-breaking and tolerance-sensitive numerical methods rather than an arbitrary finite example.
